prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy prep/verification, cold storage, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: - Medication Order Gateway: validates patient/product/dose/route/timing before downstream release; rejects incomplete updates retaining reason; routes to pharmacy; sends order status; produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. - Pharmacy Verification Station: compares order vs scanned product; blocks mismatch; Dose Exception Review Slip; Batch Release Note, audit record. - Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot: prepares only active, validly authorized orders; uses Order Reconciliation Snapshot to compare quantities vs dispense events and cabinet balances; retains order details; on exception stops, holds, preserves scans; produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. - Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler: records temperature, reports excursions/connectivity loss. - Pneumatic Tube Network: compliant loads. - East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles; East sends Tube Route Exception Ticket. - North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers: report availability, record arrivals; North uses Priority Refill Tote Tag; South reports failed lock/access. - Medication Return Kiosk: Return Bin Audit Label. Actors: - Clinical Pharmacist: exceptions, dose decisions; escalates inconclusive reviews. - Pharmacy Technician: prep, Cold Chain Handoff Card; confirms reconciliation queue clear before routine replenishment. - Hospital Courier: Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record. - Medication Safety Officer: reviews diversion/high-risk/harm events; sends Diversion Review Packet to IT Operations Specialist (checks logs, no disposition change; investigates software/connectivity faults). - Biomedical Engineer: evaluates mechanical/sensor faults, advises return to service. - Charge Nurse: Cabinet Downtime Notice; assigns open items at handover. - Registered Nurse: verifies loads, returns, no bypass. Modes: route Faulted/Available; cabinet Out of Service/Ready for Dispense. Rules: serious exceptions escalated immediately; inconclusive stays on hold; disposition records reviewer, evidence, released/corrected/withheld; reconciliation by stable order ID, timestamps; cancelled excluded; corrections supersede; duplicates flagged; partials conservative; patient/medication/quantity disagreement holds; outcome recorded for audit; returns reconciled, damaged segregated, bins secured.

New part:
S161: North Ward Cabinet Controller applies the North Ward medication access rules when evaluating a cabinet transaction.
S162: Its ward-specific configuration defines permitted medication locations, access roles, and transaction limits for each cabinet.
S163: The configuration associates each medication location with the product identifiers and quantity thresholds used by the ward.
S164: Cabinet availability is calculated from the last confirmed inventory count and subsequent recorded movements.
S165: Configured maximum and minimum quantities guide replenishment decisions without overriding an active clinical restriction.
S166: Access rules require an authenticated user role appropriate to the requested medication and transaction type.
S167: High-risk medication locations can require an additional confirmation before a removal is accepted.
S168: The controller rejects a transaction when its location mapping does not match the reconciled medication identity.
S169: Configuration changes are versioned, reviewed, and recorded with the effective time and approving authority.
S170: If the controller has not received a current approved configuration, it prevents routine dispensing and reports the condition for investigation.
S171: Bluejay maintains a time-stamped temperature history for each refrigerated medication compartment and raises an alarm when a configured limit is exceeded.
S172: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler applies approved upper and lower temperature limits to each monitored compartment.
S173: Calibrated probes report readings at configured intervals, and the cooler records probe identity and calibration status with each reading.
S174: Refrigerated stock is identified by medication, lot, and expiration date so that each unit remains traceable to its storage history.
S175: When readings exceed a limit or a probe becomes unavailable, the affected stock is marked ineligible for routine dispensing.
S176: The cooler preserves the affected stock in its current controlled environment while the condition is assessed.
S177: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler uses the handoff card to compare a transfer’s recorded custody time with its temperature history.
S178: A Clinical Pharmacist reviews excursion details and determines whether affected stock may be released, quarantined, or discarded under pharmacy policy.
S179: The cooler retains the disposition status against the affected lot and prevents stock marked ineligible from being selected for routine dispensing.
S180: Authorized access to refrigerated compartments is recorded with the user identity, access time, and affected stock identifiers.
S181: Door-open duration is monitored so that an access event that threatens temperature control can be distinguished from a brief inspection.
S182: Temperature alarms remain active during loss of network connectivity, and local records are retained until communication is restored.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
